# V3-B — the second reflexive-awareness: distinction-and-non-distinction
<hr/><div class="sub">K6 argmap (full)</div><div class="en"># IPVV — V3-B K6 ARGUMENT MAP (the Kāṇāda measures: parimāṇa / pramāṇa / unmāna, aṇu/mahat) *2026-08-11. Reconstruct *argument-by-argument* before writing prose. Source: M00022 lines 1905–1951 (IPK 2.2.6 commentary, the number/measure/samkhyā section). This is the passage that read as &quot;the measure is the cut-other-object-expecting; with the twenty-four-digit-ness, the famous, he who is the hand-manifestation…&quot;* --- ## 1. What is at issue Abhinavagupta is defending the thesis of kārikā 1 — the cognitions of action, relation, *substance*, direction, etc. are true (by stability + efficacy). In kārikā 6 he has been showing that the *conjunction* (samanvaya) of the grammatical adjuncts (kāraka) is the action-reflexive-awareness object. Now, along the way, he must deal with the *substance* (dravya) cognition, which the Vaiśeṣika grounds in **number and measure** (saṃkhyā, parimāṇa). So the whole point here is: are number and measure *real features of things* (as the Vaiśeṣika says) or *relational, conventional phenomena* (as Abhinava argues)? This is the same bhedābheda / saṃvṛti battle as before, now applied to quantity. ## 2. The argument, reconstructed step by step **Step 0 — the maxim (line 1905):** &gt; &quot;No real entity (sattvabhūto&#x27;rthaḥ) is expressed without a number.&quot; — i.e. every thing we speak of comes numbered (one, two, …). So number seems to be essential to reality. **Step 1 — number is relational, not a free-standing thing (1907–1911):** In that [numbered statement], the number-*appearance* (saṃkhyābhāsa) of the nominal-meaning takes the subordinate position (upasarjana). For it is the very nature of the case-ending-meaning (vibhaktyartha) to be a *quality* (guṇībhāva) in the nominal-meaning. Hence, with the words &quot;one,&quot; &quot;two,&quot; etc., what is grasped as primary is the *mutual-cut-appearance* (parasparāvacchedābhāsa) — the appearance of each thing as delimiting/being-delimited-by the others. And by that, the *object-form alone* is the number-with-its-two-folds [the one and the many]. &quot;Number&quot; itself, then, is just *the counting of distinctions* (bhedagaṇanātmikā) — it is not an extra real thing added to the object. **Step 2 — measure (parimāṇa) is likewise relational (1912–1940):** [Abhinava continues:] &quot;And measure, too [is such]&quot;: &gt; the atom, the great, the short, the long, and — this is the measure the Kāṇādas (Vaiśeṣikas) are famous for. Take first the short-and-long: &gt; the length, though, would be the measure… — so it [length] fits the definition of &quot;measure&quot; (pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa). Now: &quot;measure&quot; (pramāṇa) is *relative to a delimited other object* (paricchinnavastvantarāpekṣa). It is *the appearance of comparison* (samīkaraṇābhāsa): the famous hand-appearance of twenty-four digits (a cubit), with which one compares — and this is *not* a mere external conjunction (saṃyoga). Hence he says: &quot;measure too, as if by an inner-unity-part, of the to-be-measured cloth, measured by the hand — from the attainment of the conjunction [samanvaya].&quot; The taking up of the measuring-rod (yaṣṭyupādāna) is *for the sake of raising the short/long distinction*. [i.e. measure = the appearance of comparison against a standard, not a real intrinsic magnitude.] **Step 3 — atom-ness and great-ness are NOT part-less-ness (1928–1933):** But what is said — &quot;atom, great&quot;? If atom-ness (aṇutva) were *mere part-less-ness* (abhāgatāmātra), then it would belong to the part-less qualities and actions (guṇakarmādīnāṃ abhāgānām). If, on the other hand, atom-ness were the substance&#x27;s being-part-less (abhāvatva), then it would belong to space (ākāśa) too. Both fail. So: atom-ness = *the fitness to be delimited from all sides*, by the world-famous very-subtle [thing] — the lightest of the mustard-seed, the pod, the small box, the little box (sarṣapaka-vāṭapiṭikapeṭaka). That alone is atom-ness; the other [extreme] is great-ness (mahattva). [i.e. atom/mahat are relational measures of delimitation, not absolute partless/ parted natures.] **Step 4 — the three measures: parimāṇa, pramāṇa, unmāna (1935–1949):** The verse &quot;the measure, though, from all sides&quot; (parimāṇaṃ tu sarvataḥ) is what grasps this. Then: &quot;the prastha-kudava&quot; — of the to-be-measured sesame-and-the-rest, measured by the wood-cup-like, the measure whose mark is the *comparison-appearance* — not a mere conjunction; that too [is] &quot;as if by an inner-unity-part.&quot; And the &quot;unmāna,&quot; the name, is marked as the &quot;upward-measure&quot; (ūrdhvamāna = weight). The Kāṇādas say unmāna = heaviness (gurutva) causing the falling-action. But that is not so: in mere heaviness there is no measuring-dealing (mānavyavahāra). Rather, the *famous* heaviness — as by the balance-weights (prativartaka) — and its *comparison* alone is the unmāna (so the grammarians say). Thus &quot;measure-ness&quot; (mānatā) is the *same* in the three [parimāṇa, pramāṇa, unmāna]: the difference is only that the measuring is &quot;extended,&quot; &quot;around,&quot; or &quot;upward,&quot; in measure- form. And this is fit — he says &quot;the māṣaka-rakitikā&quot;: of the to-be-measured gold, measured by the balance-weight, the mark is the *heaviness-comparison-appearance*. So measure is used, as if by an inner-unity-part, in the dealing (vyavahāra) of buying and selling (krayavikraya), by the greater-and-lesser (prakarṣāpakarṣa) alone. Two examples are written down, joined by the connection. **Step 5 — separateness too (1950–1951):** Separateness (pṛthaktva), likewise, is preceded by the grasping of distinctions: it is the distinction-appearance whose middle is the un-difference that is internally conjectured (śaṅkyamāna). [And it runs] from the number-delimited &quot;one,&quot; &quot;separate,&quot; up to the &quot;separate&quot; of the far end. ## 3. Unresolved / uncertain (not invented) 1. The exact Vaiśeṣika definitions (parimāṇa vs. pramāṇa vs. unmāna) — the text presupposes the Vaiśeṣika-sūtra&#x27;s three measures; my reconstruction (parimāṇa = all-sides/volume, pramāṇa = length, unmāna = weight/upward) follows the text&#x27;s own glosses but should be checked against the Vaiśeṣika and Kāśikā. 2. The &quot;twenty-four-digit&quot; cubit and the &quot;prastha-kudava&quot; (volume measures), &quot;māṣaka-rakitikā&quot; (gold weights), &quot;sarṣapaka-vāṭapiṭikapeṭaka&quot; (mustard-pod/small-box) — realia whose exact magnitudes are technical; the *argument* (measure = comparison) is clear, the magnitudes are not. 3. &quot;diṣṭya (yaṣṭy)upādānaṃ&quot; — the reading/correction of the measuring-rod; textual. ## 4. Decision for L2 Proceed. The point is now understood: number and measure are *not* real intrinsic features — they are *relational appearances of comparison and counting* (against a standard: the cubit, the balance, the cup). Atom/great, short/long, heavy/light are all ways of *delimiting* a thing relative to others — the very bhedābheda/saṃvṛti doctrine applied to quantity. The Vaiśeṣika&#x27;s reification of measure is rejected; the realia (magnitudes) are logged, not resolved. </div><hr/><div class="sub">S7 argmap (full)</div><div class="en"># IPVV — V3-B S7 ARGUMENT MAP (the &quot;wtf&quot; passage: kriyāśakti / arthakriyā / anvaya-vyatireka) *2026-08-11. The missing move: reconstruct the passage *argument-by-argument* before writing any prose. Source: M00022 lines 975–1019 (IPK 2.2.1 commentary, the upayoga/arthakriyā section). This is the passage that read as &quot;with the dealing-mere-param-essence-ness…&quot; — i.e. not understood. Below: the explicit argument reconstruction, in plain terms, then the freestyle L2 READ. T1/L1 untouched.* --- ## 1. What is at issue **The question:** What makes a cognition &quot;true&quot; (satya)? In kārikā 1, Abhinavagupta said the action-cognitions are true by two things: their *stability* (sthairya) and their *efficacy* (upayoga, = arthakriyā, the capacity to bring about its intended effect). But &quot;efficacy&quot; is a slippery criterion. This whole passage is Abhinava testing and defending it against a Buddhist (Vijñānavāda/Sautrāntika-style) objection about the causal relation between a cognition and its object. **The Buddhist problem:** Buddhists deny that a real external object is the cause of a cognition — and they deny causal relations between momentary phenomena anyway. Abhinava wants to say: the *action- cognition* is true *because* it has causal efficacy (it gets you to the village). The Buddhist counters: causal efficacy can&#x27;t be the mark of truth, because (a) the object that would be the cause is un-graspable, and (b) momentariness makes the whole cause/effect talk incoherent. ## 2. The argument, reconstructed step by step **Step 0 — where efficacy holds.** [Abhinava, from the prior passage:] For anything, being *the cause of a given cognition* (tajjñānakāritā) is what establishes that thing&#x27;s having causal efficacy (arthakriyākāritva) and hence its being-ness (sattva). But this is *not* the case for the blue [the object] that is manifest *at the very same time* as the cognition. [i.e. the object is simultaneous with the cognition, so it can&#x27;t be its cause — a cause must precede its effect.] **Objection (nanu):** Fine — let even what is simultaneous with the manifestation be the cause. **Abhinava&#x27;s first reply:** Then we&#x27;d have to say &quot;two things of equal time stand in the cause-effect relation&quot; — which is nonsense. But that&#x27;s not really my point; it&#x27;s a secondary refutation. My real point: it is *the being-manifest* itself (bhāsamānatā) that, at that time, is the *ground* (nimitta) of calling something a cause. And that manifest-ness is no different in the case of the two-moon [an illusion]. So manifest-ness alone can&#x27;t be the mark of truth — otherwise the two-moon would be true too. **Step 1 — the positive criterion (Abhinava):** Consider the blue. That which *accompanies* the presence and absence [anvaya-vyatireka] of the blue — i.e. is present when the blue is present and absent when the blue is absent — and which is simultaneous with the appearing — *that alone* is the cause of the cognition. The presence-and-absence [anvaya-vyatireka] are both present in the blue [it tracks the real blue], and the blue existed even before the cognition (it&#x27;s not produced by the cognition). This is NOT so in the two-moon [its presence/absence doesn&#x27;t track a real object]. This, he says, is what &quot;thus&quot; (tathā) means. **Objection (nanu) — the Buddhist counters:** But that &quot;which follows the presence-and-absence, is marked by appearing, and exists before the appearing, as the blue&quot; — *that* cognition [the one that tracks this] — its manifest moment (kṣaṇa) is not [a real cause]. And then the same old flaw returns: it would still lack efficacy. [i.e. you can&#x27;t get a real cause out of a momentary manifest cognition.] **Abhinava&#x27;s reply (naca):** In *your* view, this flaw doesn&#x27;t even arise — because you hold that &quot;whatever is the cause of a cognition is what is manifested [in it].&quot; That&#x27;s perfectly non- contradictory for you [you&#x27;re an idealist — for you there&#x27;s no external object to worry about]. But consider what follows in your view: for you, the *known object*&#x27;s character of being *limited in time* (pārimityalakṣaṇa) IS time itself; and the known [object] IS just the knowing [consciousness]; and there&#x27;s no &quot;touch of time&quot; in it [no real temporal relation]; and &quot;moment&quot; (kṣaṇa) is just a convention, measured by the winking of an eye or some other action. So what relation does it have, and what does &quot;momentariness&quot; even mean? [i.e. your own position dissolves the very notions of cause, moment and time you need to press this objection.] **Objection (nanu) — sarcastic:** &quot;Now, like a poor man celebrating a festival, you&#x27;ve gone out of your way to complete the *other* [Buddhist&#x27;s] view, while your *own* view you&#x27;ve left un-filled!&quot; **Abhinava&#x27;s reply:** And it *is* filled (pūritā) — by what follows (kṣaṇabhaṅge&#x27;pi). [i.e. my view too is complete.] **Step 2 — the crux (Abhinava):** Even granting momentariness (kṣaṇabhaṅga), the argument works. If we speak in terms of the *stream* (santāna) — treating the prior and later moments as one &quot;same&quot; thing by the conceit (abhimāna) of continuity — then even so: the later moment, following immediately (after the earlier), *by that very connection* (prabandha), establishes the causal efficacy and hence the being-ness [of the action]. This the opponent has himself established — so Abhinava turns it against him (&quot;here, [you&#x27;ve] refuted your own side&quot;): &gt; &quot;When it is said that &#x27;the cognition-cause, helped by presence-and-absence, is the manifest blue,&#x27; &gt; then why is the two-moon *not* also of this kind [manifest + tracking a real object]?&quot; — this is not &gt; settled [by the opponent]. For in the non-manifestation [of the prior blue / two-moon moment], there &gt; is no difference at all between the prior blue and the two-moon-moment [both are equally &gt; un-manifested prior to the cognition]. [Here Abhinava presses: if the criterion is &quot;manifest + tracks presence/absence,&quot; then either (a) the prior blue-moment isn&#x27;t manifest and so can&#x27;t be the cause — leaving the two-moon on equal footing; or (b) if it is manifest, then the two-moon is too. Either way the Buddhist&#x27;s criterion fails.] ## 3. Unresolved / uncertain (to be checked, not invented) 1. The exact force of &quot;nīle staḥ / pūrvam abhūt eva&quot; — whether Abhinava concedes a real prior blue or only a conventional one. This bears on whether he grants the Sautrāntika an external object. [Ratié/ Torella on IPK 2.2.1 and the Buddhist opponent should adjudicate.] 2. The sarcastic &quot;poor man / festival&quot; (daridreṇeva utsavakāriṇā) — Abhinava&#x27;s wry tone; the reply &quot;and it is filled&quot; (pūritā ca) needs the next clause (kṣaṇabhaṅge&#x27;pi) to be read as completing his own view. Interpreted here as self-completion, but the exact referent of &quot;it&quot; (nijā dṛṣṭiḥ = his own view, or the other view) is worth a second look. 3. &quot;tat vijñānāt pūrvam abhūt eva&quot; — the ontology of the prior blue (realist vs idealist reading). ## 4. Decision for L2 Proceed to L2. The doctrinal spine is now *understood*: Abhinava defends &quot;efficacy = truth&quot; by showing that (i) manifest-ness alone is too weak (two-moon), (ii) the real criterion is manifest-ness *tracking presence-and-absence* of a prior, and (iii) the Buddhist&#x27;s own momentariness/stream concessions actually *support* his conclusion rather than refute it. The three unresolved points above are logged, not resolved. </div><hr/><div class="sub">S9 argmap (full)</div><div class="en"># IPVV — V3-B S9 ARGUMENT MAP (the &quot;dāntava/līvarda&quot; cow-bull passage) *2026-08-11. Reconstruct *argument-by-argument* before writing prose. Source: M00022 lines 1139–1159 (IPK 2.2.1 commentary, the saṃvṛtisatya / sāmānya section). This is the passage that read as &quot;&#x27;dāntava&#x27;-&#x27;līvarda&#x27;-and-the-rest words alone the Ārya-worldly declare the bulls.&quot;* --- ## 1. What is at issue Abhinavagupta has been distinguishing the *conventionally-true* (saṃvṛtisatya) from the *untrue* (asatya). The objector (Buddhist/Naiyāyika) tried to collapse the conventional into the merely fictional — like the double-moon — by saying: &quot;the convention-mind covers [reality], and what it covers is only what the mind itself raises; never is the actually-seen thing attributed to the universal.&quot; Abhinava refuted that. Now he must say what *positively* the conventional-true consists in — and in particular, what role the universal (sāmānya) plays in it. The cow/bull business is his example of how the universal is a *conventional* (saṃvṛti) entity, not a fiction. ## 2. The argument, reconstructed step by step **Step 0 — recap (from prior lines 1139–1149):** The objector: &quot;the convention-mind is a *coverer*: it attributes to an object what was never actually seen, such as the universal.&quot; Abhinava&#x27;s reply: &quot;not even so&quot; (nāpi). For the double-moon&#x27;s twoness is *seen* (dṛṣṭatā) — and yet the same *seen-ness* belongs equally to any one of many objects. So by this much, delusion-ness has no extra specific character. And then: even *delusion-specific-ness* is not accepted by the text-author — he declares [the pair] with a **dvandva** (coordinate compound). [The point: &quot;convention-and-delusion&quot; are named as a coordinate pair, implying they are *equal-form* (tulya- svarūpa) — i.e. the conventional is not a sub-species of delusion but something coordinate with it.] In the simultaneous-support-ness [of two equal things] there is a dvandva; and a dvandva is of the equal-own-form two alone. The universal (sāmānya), without swallowing all the specifics, operating, possessing even another specific, wishing the intended specific, crooking [it] toward itself — not separately obtaining a word-entry — [this is what the universal is]. **Step 1 — the world&#x27;s actual usage (the cow/bull point, lines 1150–1153):** The proof is *direct* (āñjasyena), by the clear world-cognition. **Here is the example:** In the Ārya-world&#x27;s actual usage, the words &quot;dāntava,&quot; &quot;līvarda,&quot; and the like are what ordinary people use to *point at bulls* (puṅgavān) — the male of the class. But the single word &quot;cow&quot; (go) refers, in the same usage, to the female-cows (strī-gavīḥ) alone. So it is with the cognition. [i.e. the word &quot;cow&quot;/&quot;go&quot; conventionally picks out a *specific* sub-class — the females — while the &quot;bull&quot;-words pick out the males; neither is a bare universal floating free of specifics.] And when someone says &quot;this city has cows&quot; (gomad idaṃ nagaram), what flashes in the mind is simply the *abundance of milk and curds* — not any claim about the sex or a free-floating &quot;cow-ness.&quot; **Step 2 — the marker of the conventional (lines 1156–1158):** &quot;The conventional-ness&quot;: the marker of the conventional is *this much and no more* (etāvanmātram) — and even the opponent, unwilling, must accept this much. That marker, along with the marked word, he indicates with &quot;that-which&quot; (yattathā). **Step 3 — why this wins (lines 1158–1161):** In this marker, with the *manifestation* and the *use* [the two criteria of the earlier discussion] removed, in the non-possibility, **our victory** (asmākaṃ jayaḥ). If, again, in the non-possibility, the *use* is scattered in the other [i.e. the opponent&#x27;s sense of use fails], then — with this intent — he first states the *other&#x27;s expectation* (parāpekṣāṃ), &quot;objection (nanu).&quot; ## 3. Unresolved / uncertain (not invented) 1. **dāntava / līvarda** — the lexemes. Argument: they&#x27;re male-class (bull) words in contrast to &quot;cow&quot; (female). Exact referents/etymology unknown (likely regionally-marked agrarian terms for castrated/male bovines). NOT resolved; the *argument* (some words pick the male, &quot;cow&quot; the female) is clear and preserved. 2. The exact force of the dvandva point: &quot;convention-and-delusion&quot; as coordinate (tulyasvarūpa) vs. the objector&#x27;s subordination — interpreted here as Abhinava denying the conventional is a sub-species of delusion. Worth a second check against the actual dvandva in the text. 3. &quot;gomad idaṃ nagaram&quot; — is this Abhinava&#x27;s example or a quoted usage? Read as his own example of the word&#x27;s practical referent (milk-and-curds), i.e. the conventional&#x27;s *arthakriyā*. ## 4. Decision for L2 Proceed. The point is now understood: the universal/cow is a *conventional* entity whose whole reality is &quot;this much&quot; — the practical, world-bound tracking of a sub-class — not a fiction and not a bare Platonic universal. The world&#x27;s own usage (bull-words vs. cow-word) proves the universal is always anchored in specifics. The cow-possessing-city example shows the conventional&#x27;s &quot;meaning&quot; is its practical upshot (milk, curds). Unresolved lexemes logged, not resolved. </div><hr/><div class="sub">full L2 (full)</div><div class="en"># IPVV — V3-B kārikās 1–7: L2 READ (full reference unit) *2026-08-11. The complete READ prose for the dvitīyo vimarśa (IPK 2.2.1–2.2.7), derived from the L1 controlled translation. This is the publication test: does one complete IPVV argument survive conversion from Sanskrit-close controlled English into readable prose while remaining propositionally traceable and epistemically honest? L2 rules per `CALIBRATION_REPORT.md`: preserve every proposition, add no new doctrine, dissolve `-ness`, unpack compounds, break impossible sentences, recover referents only from context, keep objection/reply structure, surface rather than invent external-knowledge gaps, and never make an obscure passage sound falsely clear. Every sentence is traceable to L1 spans → L0 → Sanskrit. The small `L2_CHANGE_LOG` is at the end. T1 golden chunks untouched.* --- # V3-B — the second reflexive-awareness: distinction-and-non-distinction ## Kārikā 1 — the action-cognitions are true, by stability and efficacy The cognitions of action, relation, universal, substance, direction and time have a substrate that is at once one and many, and they are to be accepted as true — true by their stability and true by their efficacy. Abhinavagupta begins by considering the cognition of action in particular. A cognition of action that arises apart from the very essence of consciousness is an appearance of action: it is of a form both one and many, it is cut off by the power of māyā, and it takes the essence of action as its object. Such a cognition is grounded in the true alone. For it is stable — no refutation uproots it — and it agrees with what subsequently follows: in the case intended, the attainment of the village is precisely the end that this cognition helps bring about. A real entity, in producing its effect, takes on both difference and non-difference, and it is the bearer of this agreement with what follows. In that situation, what is the &quot;form&quot; of the thing? The form is that which is the thing&#x27;s own nature, unswerving from it. And the &quot;action&quot; is what, by the force of its appearance, makes even what is not its own nature take on its own nature — that which clings to the form and shapes it. Here is the example Abhinavagupta gives. The body of Caitra — and of Maitra — although it differs according to this or that place, time and shape, nevertheless shines forth without ever abandoning its oneness, in the recognition &quot;this is the very same body.&quot; That very unity is the action, in the judgment &quot;Caitra is walking.&quot; And in an action that has thus become established, the act of grasping &quot;there goes Caitra&quot; is experienced as continuing — nothing uproots it — and it serves that action in the intended attainment of the village. Abhinavagupta then draws the decisive line. He holds firmly that it is being-manifest, and nothing else, that constitutes the form of things — not the doing of an effect. It is the doing of an effect that he now examines, at length, in what follows. He asks whether this doing-of-an-effect is to be identified with the thing&#x27;s own nature — whether by identity and by the absence of deviation, or by deviation from a common dharma; whether it is the thing&#x27;s very form, or its defining mark, or a mere incidental indicator standing near a mark. He settles: &quot;own-form&quot; is spoken here only metaphorically. For just as &quot;having branches&quot; is what we point to when we speak of tree-ness — a mere exclusion, since the words are synonyms — so in the world it is not said that the unreal does the effect; that would not be known, because of the synonymy. And it is not the defining mark either, as he shows by adding &quot;and it is marked.&quot; ## Kārikā 2 — the one inner essence enters the many An objector interjects. &quot;Still,&quot; he says, &quot;your reason is not established: the specific condition of &#x27;not being refuted&#x27; is impossible for it. For you have declared that the substances and the rest are one-and-many in nature — the very same thing is both one and many. How is that a refutation? This is in fact your own objection, raised to be refuted.&quot; To this Abhinavagupta replies: &gt; There, the one — the inner essence — attaining the organ-known-ness, &gt; goes into the many-ness, by its place-time-own-nature. Consider the action, and the rest. Once their truth is established, the one-ness and many-ness spoken of — even when subordinated in the Vṛtti — are to be established here as the primary thing to be known. Reflecting on this, Abhinavagupta makes the determination. Between the one-ness and the many-ness, he takes the one-ness: &quot;this way it is established; and the many-ness, this way.&quot; Of the blue and the other beings, the inner essence is the supreme essence, marked by consciousness alone. There is no counting there, because of its dense non-difference — not even of its one-ness, since that one-ness, there, has no separate being. But what is inner — unmixed with other appearances, going within — and inner, known by the inner organ alone — that is the one essence. That one, again, without losing its one-ness, attains its being-known by the external organ, and by the distinction of place and the rest — &quot;here and there, now and then, thin and not-thin&quot; — it goes into the many-ness. There is no contradiction in this, because the cognition is not broken. It is like the relation of cause and non-cause: the distinction of objects can be spoken of only insofar as we are dealing with their mere essential nature. Hence there is no contradiction at all between the one-ness and the many-ness; &quot;Caitra moves,&quot; in the action; and so in the remaining cases. ## Kārikā 3 — the mind-re-determination makes the conceptions Another objection. &quot;From the distinction of objects you say &#x27;one, many.&#x27; By what is this to be grasped? Take the case of the eye. With the eye-experience, first of all, Caitra manifests as divided by the distinction of place alone; this cognition has no capacity to mix the appearance-distinctions together, because it does not investigate. So they say. But with the construction — the mental operation — the object is not truly touched at all.&quot; To this the answer is given in the sūtra: &gt; These cognitions, supporting the two [one and many], the mind re-determining, being, &gt; make the conceptions of action and the rest — conceptions made of the knower&#x27;s operation. Here, although even in the un-constructed perception — in the mere manifestation of &quot;it is,&quot; or of &quot;it is a jar&quot; — the universal and the rest have their appearance, in the extended grasping, and even, for the yogin, the action-manifestation and the time-manifestation could be spoken of; still, in that state, the universal and the rest do not attain their own life. For the &quot;life&quot; of the appearances of the universal, the relation, the action, the substance and the direction is this: the staining by the universal; the rising of the distinction among the things related; the grasping of the unity of the streaming moments; the making of the part-mass; the manifestation of the limited in the limit. And this life is clearly manifested only in the construction. And the construction of the mind is manifested in the re-determination — at the occasion of the māyā-bound knower. By that mind, acting as the agent, making the re-determination — the reflective awareness that follows the direct manifestation of an object — the action, the relation and the rest become its object. As will be said, in the one-utterance-object, the cognition is such-and-such. The prefix &quot;anu-&quot; (&quot;re-&quot;), Abhinavagupta explains, means &quot;after&quot; (paścāt): &quot;the mind alone makes the conceptions.&quot; This is the connection. The sentence runs: &quot;of that, its own form is specifically marked, &#x27;the instrument,&#x27; to the end; the two participial endings, however, carry the seed of a reason, in the making of the conception.&quot; Between which two does the mind stand, in the Vṛtti? Having doubted, he shows: &quot;of the grasped and the grasper,&quot; and &quot;external and the rest,&quot; &quot;of that, to the end,&quot; with the sentence. &quot;With the knower together, the distinction and the relation rest in their absence from one another, and cannot be dealt with — of which two.&quot; &quot;Of that,&quot; of the knower. Here, the reason, he gives: &quot;of the knower.&quot; The knower — determining the object, the external and the inner, the to-be-constructed, with varied joinings — that very object is said to be the action, the universal and the rest. &quot;He deals&quot; — he makes the joining of the Vṛtti, &quot;the mental-ness, and the rest.&quot; &quot;The reason&quot; — the remainder of the three sentences. An objection: &quot;Who, then, is another knower…&quot; — answered, as will be said, by the verse &quot;if not, the inner-made…&quot; (1.3.7), and the rest. &quot;The impression-born&quot;: for the impression indeed culminates in the unity of the knower, as is said. Hence, as the Buddhists think of the experience-impression-born cognition, so here it does not become the case — this is to be thought. &quot;And in the eye and the rest,&quot; to the end, &quot;the resting-ness, to the end&quot; — the intention has been explained at the very beginning of the sūtra-explanation. And here, with the grasping of the &quot;universal,&quot; everything, the relation and the rest, is marked by it. &quot;The universal-form even&quot;: the un-clear-more, is the meaning. &quot;The universal is said&quot;: not &quot;the universal,&quot; they are dealt with. Here, to give room to the reason — &quot;of them, and the rest&quot; — and to the to-be-said, for the manifestation of the universal&#x27;s own form, he says: &quot;of the specific-ones, following, to the end.&quot; Another objection: &quot;Here, at this occasion, he — the one-alone-appearance — what is to be said? Not, first, &#x27;the universal,&#x27; which you alone declared.&quot; Answer: &quot;thus alone, the being-jar…&quot; (2.3.5), in this. Now, how is it said that &quot;in the mixing with other appearances alone is the object-action&quot;? Here, the answer is: &quot;place, and the rest.&quot; Here, now: &quot;the &#x27;is,&#x27; i.e. the being-manifestation, the mere thus-ness, has become the own-marker&quot; — with the appearances of form, blue, and the rest, which are the external limb, and which in the own-marker-ness are no helpers, what deed is there? Without the two appearances of place and time, not even with a thousand appearances, in the mixing, does the own-marker-ness come to an end: &quot;the blue, the cloth, the extended, the cotton, the soft, the thin,&quot; and so on, from the flashing of the mere universal-form. But &quot;this-that&quot; — the mixing of the appearances of place and time — removes the universal-form. Hence that alone is the inner limb, in the coming-to-be of own-marker-ness. This very point he establishes: &quot;of the two alone,&quot; of the two, place and time, in their form of east and west, and the rest. The place is marked by the far and the near; the variety of the prior and the later… The point about usage. With the camasa cup they bring the rice; he sprinkles the ṣoḍaśin; he takes it — and the rest. Even so, the word is not able to make known the specific, the present- manifestation. The meaning that is perceived from the word, without the help of a pointing finger and the rest, is perceived as the place-time-un-cut alone — this is the meaning that is established without effort. And this will be so in the valid-means-marker. With this much, the re-determination-operation alone revives the essence of the universal, the action, and the rest. That which is current, that he determines and summarizes: &quot;thus, and.&quot; &quot;In this,&quot; where the own-marker and universal-form are fit for reflection, such a case. &quot;Not then,&quot; at the time of the mental determination. &quot;The universal,&quot; in this very word — the cut. Here, the reason: &quot;place and the rest&quot;; the connection even, &quot;then&quot;; the action even, &quot;then&quot; — the connection. The other sentence is of the form of a reason. &quot;The said,&quot; &quot;the mind-re-determining,&quot; &quot;the conceptions,&quot; and — &quot;will be said&quot;: &quot;… the constructions support the two&quot; (2.2.5). This is the third verse. Thus, with this much, in the convention, in the construction-mind, of the flashing universal and the rest: the conventional being-ness, the name — the being-ness-specific alone — stands; not, as in the case of the double-moon and the rest, the un-truth — this is established. Here is how the matter is brought into order. Of consciousness — marked by the reflective awareness of freedom, and the unfolded effect of the action-power — that which is the relation, the universal, and the rest. There even, the relation-form alone — marked by the many-one form — is, everywhere, the essential form. There, though, with the joining of the un-common other form, there is the other name. &quot;Of the many-individual-mass, he who is the unity-own, the relation — there, &#x27;cows,&#x27; with the tolerance of the other designation.&quot; There, the universal-speech, in the flow of many moments, from the strength of its support, becomes one; &quot;moves,&quot; with the strength of the designation, is the action-dealing; &quot;of the threads-one-ness, &#x27;this is the cloth,&#x27;&quot; the substance-dealing; &quot;of the childhood-and-the-rest-states-one-ness,&quot; the state-possessor-dealing. Thus elsewhere. &gt; the relation whose self is distinction-and-non-distinction, established in all objects; &gt; the world-path… (ślo. 1) This is said in the establishment of the relation. Even by the holders of divided universals, of the inherence, of the relation, &quot;it helps&quot; — &quot;the relation,&quot; by the rule, with the relation, or, of the helped, from the acceptance. And the relation, made of the one-many, having the freedom of the knower as its self, by the glory of the action-power. Hence the relation alone is the root in the establishment of the unity of the knower: &gt; &quot;… in the relation, the attentiveness&quot; (vi. bhai. 106) of the statement. That very point, to investigate, Abhinavagupta states the sūtra: ## Kārikā 4 — the relation is the mutual form-clinging in the one knower &gt; The beings, resting in the self, distinct-manifestation, in the one knower, &gt; joined by a unity that is the form of mutual relation — these are the word of the &gt; relation-cognition. &quot;The king&quot; and &quot;the person,&quot; because they are distinct, are manifested as external. Hence, when they partake of unity, in the one knower, in the completion, in that very form, in the own self alone. And that unity is not a bare unity — not the melting of the own-form — because the relation would then be impossible; but it is the mutual clinging of forms, the simultaneous drowning and emerging, the two phases of distinction-and-non-distinction, of the form of a swinging machine — this is the mark of the relation. And that too is not exclusively with the knower; but mutually — &quot;of the king, the person,&quot; or, of that, &quot;the king.&quot; Merely, in the attainment of that-being, the touch of consciousness of these is accepted as a mere means, like the fire that, in the mingling of the gold-drop, does not at all break its own form. The two, being joined with a unity of that sort — the two beings — are the word, and the object, of the relation-cognition &quot;of the king, the person,&quot; and so on. Everywhere, the relation is two-resting-alone: &gt; &quot;with that self alone, of that, would be — how — with the breath, the control&quot; (ślo. 21) This is it. Thence, even in the māyā-bound standing, in the distinction, by the glory of manifestation, the non-distinction does not deviate. &quot;One-one&quot;: he alone is the operation of the māyā-bound knower, by which that being-two, of the relation-form, is created, and manifested, and reflected. &quot;The distinct&quot;: from the prior, of the relation-less state, the distinct-marker — the meaning. Thence alone, with the operation of the construction, connected with the knower, from its being unveiled, with the known-ness by the inner organ, from its un-common-ness, with the distinction of knowers, of the being, in the variety of the relation, the relation-state, and, becoming, is not flawed. &quot;Somewhere, in the appearance-part indeed, the param-Lord, sometimes, mixes the knowers, and he unjoins the others, and the rest&quot; — this is said many times. An objection: &quot;The mere made-ness of distinction-and-non-distinction is the mark of the relation, with the primary-and-secondary quality, of the two related…&quot; ## Kārikā 5 — the class and substance manifestations are one-form outside too Continuing the investigation of the relation, Abhinavagupta now turns to the class and substance appearances. Even granted that the relation is a mixture of unity and non-unity, the class- appearances have their own distinctive character; and to state the further distinction he introduces the sūtra: &gt; Of the class-substance-appearances, the one-form obtains outside as well; &gt; and the constructions also grasp the distinction among individuals and their parts. Consider the class-appearances — the appearances, that is, whose essence is appearance itself, the classes. The constructions that grasp them and reflect on them — the construction-minds — do not merely take up the unity within: they also set up the mere non-unity outside. Insofar as, outside as well, by the one-cow-ness running through them, the unity — that which grounds the use of the single nominal word and helps the use of the plural word — and the distinction, which belongs to the individual and necessarily supports the grasping of the individual: these constructions grasp, manifest and reflect all this in the form &quot;these cows,&quot; facing outward, taking the non-difference as the qualifier and the difference as the qualified, in the very act of cognition. So too with the substance-appearances: the constructions, outside as well, take up the one-form and the distinction of parts — &quot;jar,&quot; as the un-knotted one, with its extended-ness, of the many-part… &gt; &quot;of the other self, that which is the self, is manifested as that-self-like&quot; (vā. pa. 3.3.9) This is it. &quot;Thence alone&quot; — that is, because the one-many form is not manifested in the eye-seen in this way — is said at length; &quot;thence from the reason,&quot; is the sense. &quot;Would be,&quot; with the reason, is conceivable: first, from the present-object-appearance of the eye-seen, of the universal and the part-possessor and the rest, with its all-common-ness and clarity, even then from its presence. When the sage Kaṇāda says: &gt; &quot;from the inherence in form-substance, the eye-seen, the universals&quot; (4.1.11) This is it. &quot;From the un-manifestation,&quot; taking the distinction-own-form-marker as primary, from the resting of the cognition — the sense. &quot;Caitra.&quot; Although even the jar and the rest are agreed to be the part-possessor, and thus he will say &quot;from the other sesame, and the rest&quot;; still, &quot;this-I, this much, I go, I stand&quot; — this was said to show that the recollection of oneness has no deviation, in any manner, in the living body. &quot;The jar indeed, like the house, the chariot, the village, the army and the rest, even being of an aggregate nature, could be the doer of a single effect&quot; — this is the conceivability. &quot;The childhood and the other states&quot;: not here is the continuity of the states intended, in the part-possessor-mind, since that would be no help; but &quot;this-much-I, this now, from the prior form, with this much, the distinct-extended, the un-knotted&quot; — here is the intention. Thence alone, with the divided, the part-p[ossessor]… Then, with the &#x27;ḍatar&#x27;-ending reading and the &#x27;ḍa&#x27; substitution, &quot;one-of-them.&quot; &quot;The cognizer&quot;: the utterer and the cognizer are both intended here. &quot;The doing of the cognition, in the utterer; the teaching of the cognition, in the cognizer; the bringing of the cognition.&quot; This is what is said: &quot;by the utterer, beginning with the black [cow], when the cow is present in the heart and the word is applied, then, even with the white cow in view, if the cognizer brings the cow, or even the kapila- colored one — both count as makers.&quot; If that un-fixedness did not hold, how would this work? And from the un-fixedness, the cognition of all the own-markers is established without effort. &quot;Where,&quot; in the chariot-appearance. &quot;Immediately alone,&quot; by the rule of the king-and-person relation. &quot;With the conjunction,&quot; with the non-inherence-cause-ness, being manifested, with… &gt; &quot;from the far, the one-dense, the forest&quot; like-that. Of the many, in the simultaneous grasping, with the interior not grasped, this-way alone the appearance fits, from fitness, &quot;the coarse, the one-dense&quot;; not-in-truth, otherwise. Thence, in the appearance, of the external, this is the dharma, manifesting; or, of the appearance alone, in the with-form-consciousness view, of the cognition-form-marker, this is the dharma; not of the external — this is it. This thus-appearance, &quot;the part-possessor-appearance,&quot; is not fit to say. Thus, the perception — the valid-means — which the other side showed, in the part-possessor-establishment: &gt; &quot;the all-non-grasping, from the part-possessor-establishment&quot; (nyā. 2.1.34) with the sūtra, that is rejected. Now: &gt; &quot;from the holding-drawing-fitness, and too&quot; (nyā. 2.1.35) This is it; that which was said by inference, that too he rejects, making the reason otherwise- established: &quot;the atom-aggregate, and the rest.&quot; &quot;From the variety of natures,&quot; of the jar and the rest, those which are the atoms, of them, with the strength of their own cause, with the that-being- following, from the birth; and of the jar and the rest, those which are the enjoyers, their actions, there, the superintending-condition. The &#x27;vā&#x27;-word, in the aggregation. And this, even by the part- possessor-holder, of the conjunctions, of the non-inherence-causes, for the protection, in the wind- conjunction-and-the-rest, is of-necessity-accepted as the cause, in the non-production of the rise- division-beginning-action. Thus, the establishing valid-means having been rejected, he shows the refuting [means] in the part-possessor: &quot;one, and the rest.&quot; This is the own-form-come, the refuter. Even through the holding-quality-prior-starting-dharma-face, he addresses him: &quot;the two-atom, and the rest.&quot; Thus alone, the thread-gone… With the holding, with the excess of the balance, in the cloth, the more-more of the balance, the bending would be. Here, in the prior view, the counter-measure is said. There, in brief, first, all this he refutes: &quot;would-be, and the rest,&quot; &quot;the objects, to the end.&quot; &quot;This is the flaw&quot; — the establishing-non-being, the refuting-being, the form. Now, this very point he makes clear: &quot;thus, and,&quot; in this brief, the standing — the meaning. &quot;And by the other, &#x27;of the atoms, the aggregate alone, this-way, shines&#x27;&quot; — that which is said; there, in the aggregate-appearance, the famous, that which is the divided-appearance-ness, the interior-non-grasping-raised-conjunction, the name, from the co-helper alone, from the pervasion-ness, the one-juice-distinction-emerging, the pervading; that he shows: &quot;the mass.&quot; That non-apprehension, in the current, he fits: &quot;this-which-is-the-Caitra- appearance, and the rest.&quot; Objection: &quot;if, the one alone…&quot; ## Kārikā 6 — the kāraka-conjunction is the action-reflexive-awareness-object Even in the action-adjunct relation, the distinction and the non-distinction are reflected upon, with the sūtra; and, along with that, the own-form of the direction and the rest: &gt; The conjunction of the adjuncts has the action-reflexive-awareness as its object; &gt; the direction-and-the-rest cognition is supported by the relation of the limited to the limit. &quot;The not-elsewhere-being-marker, the cause-ness&quot; — here, this is the object-meaning. In the Vṛtti- sentence too, thus. &quot;The adjunct&quot;: the substance, and the power. &quot;This is the joining: of the power- supporting, of the substances, that which is the conjunction — he, with the joining-glue-place, is the cause of the action-recollection, as, of the valid-means-known two, the cognition-cause; and the cognition, the knower-rest-ness&quot; — this is it, in the agent, in the consciousness-form, that which is the un-distinction-attainment, of the divided even, of the adjuncts, he alone is the conjunction. Thus, of the wood, the pot and the rest, in the cooking-agent, is to be said. Thus, of the adjunct- powers even, the conjunction, ending in the agent-rest-alone, with the action-face, from its unfolding; and of the action, in the agent, from the rest. Thus, of the action, with the own-marker- expectation and with the first-adjunct-expectation, that which is the distinction; and that which is, with the one-agent-rest, with the result-un… &gt; &quot;the action-relation…&quot; (2.2.1) and the rest. There, of the action alone, first, establishing the distinction and the non-distinction two, with the adjunct-face, he states the distinction, first: &quot;of the adjuncts, and the rest.&quot; &quot;With the that-form-stain-entry, the action is manifested&quot; — this is it, the distinction-form-ness, of this. Thus, he states, in the adjunct-vārtika: &gt; &quot;the divided, of the cooking, the own-form, with the adjunct-distinction, of that-mind&quot; This is it, of the action-mind. Now, the non-distinction even, he states: &quot;and &#x27;cooks,&#x27;&quot; with the &#x27;ca&#x27;-word, aggregating the non-distinction together with the distinction. &quot;&#x27;Cooks,&#x27;&quot; there, in the recollection: of the action-mind, the un-distinction-object-ness; since, this-form, the cooking- freedom-made, he who is the agent, with the that-one-possessed-ness, she, the action, with that mind, is objectified. And of that, of the agent, the one-form-ness, is the param-essence. This is what is said: &quot;with the woods, with the pot, the rice-gruel, &#x27;Caitra cooks&#x27;&quot; — the sentence-known meaning; she, in-truth, is the action. Thence-alone, &quot;the verb-word, the sentence,&quot; is said, by this honorable- one. And there, the wood-gone burning-and-the-rest; the pot-gone heating-and-the-rest; the rice-grain- gone splitting-and-the-rest — that which is, that, &quot;the cooking-form, thus,&quot; with the distinction, in the recollection, flashes even; in the Caitra-consciousness-freedom-rest, the un-distinction alone ends. This known-object he summarizes: &quot;the action-mind even.&quot; Not alone the relation-mind is the many-object — the &#x27;api&#x27;. Objection: &quot;previously-alone…&quot; &gt; &quot;the with-order-ness, and, of the worldly, of the action…&quot; (2.1.2) This is it. &quot;The true; this, though, otherwise, of the distinction, the determination.&quot; Then he says: &quot;not-alone.&quot; &quot;From the agent-unity, and,&quot; — not alone, from the result-unity, the meaning. Thus, the action, the one-many-form, having established, of the Vṛtti-sentence, &quot;the mind, to the end,&quot; of the that-explained, of the verse-half, the current meaning, with the intention, he explains: &quot;there,&quot; in the Vṛtti-sentence, in the verse-half. &quot;The adjunct-ness-mind even, that which is, she, of the divided even, of the adjunct-substances, becoming, the one-object even, the many-object&quot; — &quot;in the adjunct- ness, the mind,&quot; this, here, is said. Of the action-adjunct-ness-non-being-cognition, and of the remainder-relation-cognition, in the one-many-object-ness, in the equal, the distinction-ness, he states: &quot;of the king,&quot; &quot;the cognition, the meaning.&quot; Objection: &quot;in the remainder-relation even, the action-adjunct-prior-ness is said,&quot; having doubted… &gt; &quot;not, without the number, anyone, the being-become, the meaning, is declared&quot; This is it. There, though, of the nominal-meaning, the number-appearance attains the adjunct-being. For of the case-ending-meaning, this is the own-nature: that which is, in the nominal-meaning, the quality-becoming. Thence, with the &#x27;one&#x27;-and-the-rest words, the mutual-cut-appearance, with the primary-ness, is recollected. And by that, the object-form alone, the number-and-its-distinction-own. The number, though, the distinction-counting-own, is said. &quot;The measure even&quot;: &gt; &quot;the atom, the great, the short, the long, and&quot; This is it, that which is the measure, of the Kāṇādas, the famous; there, the short-long, this first: &gt; &quot;the length, though, the measure, would be…&quot; the measure-marker-attained. And the measure, the name, is the cut-other-object-expecting; with the twenty-four-digit-ness, the famous, he who is the hand-appearance, with him, he who is the comparison-appearance, not, outside, the conjunction-mere; that. Thence-alone, he says: &quot;the measure even,&quot; with the inner-unity-part, of the to-be-measured, of the cloth, with the expecting, with the hand, from the conjunction-attainment — the yard-stick-taking, for the raising of the short-long- distinction. &quot;The atom-great, however,&quot; — that which is said; there, the atom-ness, if the part-less- ness-mere, that, of the quality-action-and-the-rest, of the part-less, would be. Now, of the substance, the part-less-ness — the atom-ness; then, of the space even, would be. Thence, with the very-subtle-ness, with the famous, from the mustard-pod-gram-box-small-box, the lightest-alone, that which is, from all sides, the cut-fit-ness, that very is the atom-ness; the other, the great-ness… &gt; &quot;… the measure, though, from all sides&quot; with this, it is grasped. Then he says: &quot;the prastha-kudava,&quot; of the to-be-measured, of the sesame- and-the-rest, with the expecting, with the wood-cup-like, everywhere, the measure-comparison- appearance-marker, that which is the measure; not-in-truth, the conjunction-mere; that even, with the inner-unity-part. And that which is the unmāna, the name, &quot;the upward-measure,&quot; is marked; that, by the Kāṇādas, the weight-alone, the falling-action-maker, is said; not-in-truth, thus, not, it becomes, in the weight-mere, the measure-dealing-non-being; but, the famous, that which is, with the moment- and-the-rest, the weight; that-comparison alone, the unmāna, is fit — the grammarians. And thus, the measure-ness, the name, in the three, is the same. &quot;The extended, the around, with the upward-ness, or,&quot; the measure, here, with the measure-form-ness, the specific. This very, and, is fit he says: &quot;the māṣaka-rakitikā.&quot; Of the to-be-measured, of the gold… ## Kārikā 7 — the object-attainment only through the distinction-un-distinction meaning Here, &quot;the being-ness-relation, the being-ness,&quot; is struck by the under-extension, the regress, the purposelessness; &quot;the object-action, however,&quot; is the different-locus; &quot;the that-making-ness&quot; is not the always; with the cognition-birth, &quot;the thus-ness, the always, even,&quot; is not fit, like the sprout, of the seed, in the own-cognition-born, the un-wished, with the anvaya-vyatireka-grasping-non-being, from the cause-ness-non-determination; &quot;the object-action-making-fit-ness, in the true-false two, is hard-to-determine; with the other object-action, the regress; and of all, of this, in the non-manifestation, the hare&#x27;s-horn-similarity&quot; — this is it. &quot;The being-manifested-ness alone, the un-uprooted-reflexive-awareness, is the being-ness. And she, of the relation-and-the-rest, the un-alarming-alone.&quot; In the standing even, if anyone would say, &quot;from the hard-to-grasp: the world, first, desires the object-action; she, what is, of the relation-and-the-rest?&quot; — of that objector, the heart, he comforts: &gt; Thus indeed the object-attainment would be, of the object-action-desiring mother; &gt; with the distinction-un-distinction-possessing meaning, by that, not the delusion, this-form. &quot;If the true you perceive: that, with the distinction-un-distinction-made, with the relation, without, not any, in the dealing-ground, is the object-action. Where even he is not cognized, there even, of- necessity, the inner-flashing alone sits.&quot; For: the pleasure-and-the-rest, desiring, this way he would desire, if he would know that; and thus he would know, if that-very, that, would be; and still, the un-desirable would be, of that, from the accomplishment. Thence, this is the fallen, the un-crossable: &quot;that which is, of the that-not-that-form two, the distinction-un-distinction-made-ness, the relation/universal-and-the-rest-form.&quot; And this, if the untrue; what-now, the true, is said? By that, whoever here does the delusion-dealing, he alone is the other, the deluded. &quot;That,&quot; in the grasping-sūtra two, the stability-use two, are fit-alone — the sūtra-meaning. ### The ||2|| colophon &quot;Thus, in the Śrī-mahāmāheśvara-Śrīmad-ācārya-Abhinavagupta-composed, in the Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī, in the action-section, the distinction-un-distinction-reflexive- awareness, the second vimarśa.&quot; This closes the dvitīyo vimarśa. --- ## L2_CHANGE_LOG (small editorial log — not a giant apparatus) | # | type | kārikā | what happened | |---|------|--------|---------------| | 1 | major supplied referent | 1 | &quot;and of Maitra&quot; T1 chunk untouched; this is a pure derivation.* --- ## Scope Chunk lines 24–61 (the whole of kārikā 1&#x27;s commentary). Discourse segments: - S1: the root kārikā (verse, lines 26–27) - S2: IPVV commentary on kriyābuddhi / sthairya (line 29, opening) - S3: IPVV commentary, the &quot;Caitra is walking&quot; example (line 29, the tathāhi passage) ← Ratié overlap - S4: quotation vi. bhai. 106 (line 31) - S5: IPVV commentary, ābhāsamānataiva / arthakriyākāritva (line 33) - S6: quotation &quot;bāhye&#x27;py arthe...&quot; (line 35) - S7: IPVV commentary, the arthakriyā / sattva investigation + nanu/reply (lines 37–39) - S8: quotation 2.2.4 + IPVV on the satyapada / karmadhāraya (lines 41–47) - S9: IPVV commentary, the saṃvṛti / bhrānti discussion (lines 49–61) --- ## L1_READABLE — continuous English (one segment per block) ### S1 — root kārikā (ĪPK 2.2.1) The cognitions of action, relation, universal, substance, direction and time — whose substrate is both unitary and plural — are to be regarded as true, because of [their] stability and [their] efficacy. ### S2 — the cognition of action as grounded elsewhere than in consciousness Whatever cognition of action arises apart from the very essence of consciousness — an appearance of action that is of a form both one and many, cut off by the power of māyā, and which takes the essence of action as its object — that cognition is grounded in the true alone. For it is stable (not uprooted by any refuter) and it carries agreement [with subsequent experience]: in the intended [case], the attainment of the village is the very operation it helps to bring about. For a real entity, in bringing about its effect, accepts both difference and non-difference, and it is the carrier of agreement. In that [case], that which is the own-form of it, un-deviable, is precisely the &quot;form&quot; (mūrti); and what, by the force of its appearance, makes even a non-own-form become its own-form — that, clinging to the form, is the &quot;action.&quot; ### S3 — the &quot;Caitra is walking&quot; example Thus: the body of Caitra [and] Maitra, though divided by this and that place, time and shape, shines without ever abandoning its oneness in the form &quot;this is the very same [body].&quot; That very [unity] is the action, in the form &quot;Caitra is walking.&quot; And in an action that has thus become [real], the grasping (vimarśa) &quot;Caitra is going&quot; is experienced as continuing, as not uprooted by anything; and it is the helper, in the intended attainment of the village, of that [action]. ### S4 — quotation (Vīrāvalī-Bhairava 106) &quot;… in the connection [there is] the attentiveness (sāvadhānatā).&quot; ### S5 — being-manifest alone is the form, not the causal efficacy Holding in the heart that it is the being-manifested-alone which is the form of things — not the doing of an effect (arthakriyākāritva) — [Abhinavagupta] examines that doing-of-an-effect, saying &quot;here,&quot; and the rest, down to &quot;and it will be said,&quot; with a rich context. There he investigates whether the doing-of-an-effect [is], of the being, by identity and by un-deviating-dharma-ness, or by deviating-dharma-ness, the own-form, or the marker (lakṣaṇa), or — as operating near a marker — the upalakṣaṇa, or whatever. There, &quot;own-form-ness&quot; he declares to be metaphorical (aupacārika), saying &quot;from the metaphor.&quot; For [just as] &quot;having branches&quot; alone is the tree-ness — a mere exclusion by synonym-form-ness [of the word] — so it is not [said] in the world, &quot;the unreal does the effect,&quot; [because of] the non-known-ness by synonym-ness. And it is not [the case that it is] marker-ness, he shows, saying &quot;and it is marked.&quot; ### S6 — quotation &quot;even in the external meaning, thence, the distinction of the two, the manifesting meaning and its [cognition]…&quot; ### S7 — causal efficacy as sattva; the objection and reply And there, with the making-cognition of that [thing], the doing-of-an-effect of a cause is established as its being-ness (sattva) for anyone; but not [the doing-of-an-effect] of what is manifest at the same time as that cognition, of the blue. [Objection:] &quot;Let even what is simultaneous with the manifestation be the cause.&quot; Here this very point must first be said: &quot;of two of equal time there is the effect-cause relation&quot; — but this is not said [as the answer]; rather, for the arrangement of the other known object, it is a further refutation. Here he says: &quot;equal,&quot; for it is the being-manifested-alone that, at that time, is the cause in the dealing of cause-ness; and that is undifferentiated in the two-moon too — such is the sense. Now: &quot;of the two, the blue, that which is not manifesting while the anvaya and vyatireka both exist, simultaneous with the manifestation, that very one is the cognition-cause; the two [anvaya and vyatireka] are present in the blue; that, from the cognition, existed before alone; but not in the two-moon&quot; — this he says [with] &quot;thus.&quot; ### S8 — the true-word, the compound He shows &quot;the relation,&quot; and the rest, &quot;forward,&quot; citing &quot;the self-resting (svātmaniṣṭhā), the distinct-manifestation…&quot; (2.2.4) and the rest of the sūtras. Of the word &quot;true&quot; he shows the exclusion, saying &quot;from the being-manifested-ness alone.&quot; [Objection:] &quot;Truth-ness is to be said of the object, not of the appearances, of the object-bearers; how then the karmadhāraya?&quot; — &quot;Not [so]: &#x27;the true appearances&#x27; is a ṣaṣṭhī-compound, fitting in a single sentence, of the relation and the rest, by the primary/metaphorical distinction, from the simultaneous appearances, because of the joining of difference and non-difference.&quot; This he removes, saying &quot;with the appearance-truth-ness alone&quot;; this metaphor is not [merely] a metaphor; for with respect to the māyā-word this is a metaphor — as is said: &gt; &quot;from the Lord-superintended-ness the Lord alone is everything.&quot; Thus, then, here there is no distinction at all between the appearance and what is manifested. Then he says &quot;from the that-form-ness&quot;; thus even in the māyā-word, the param-essence-word not being abandoned, [it is] explained with the karmadhāraya. Now, taking the bahuvrīhi-side, supporting the māyā-word alone, he explains, &quot;or (athavā).&quot; &quot;Of these, though, of the relation and the rest&quot; — &quot;he even (so&#x27;pi), the use&quot;; &quot;thence alone, with our established rules, that which is the object-action-use; thence-from-that-reason, with the different reference, the &#x27;tas&#x27; fifth [cases] are to be joined; otherwise the two &#x27;eva&#x27;-words would be simply disconnected.&quot; &quot;These (ete),&quot; the relation and the rest. This very [point] he fits, saying &quot;convention.&quot; &quot;With what speech are they, [the relation and the rest], separately declared, from the sensory, and from the mental, from the delusion?&quot; He says: &quot;thus, and.&quot; For if the distinction-ness of the conventional-being were wished [to hold] by the delusion-form, then that would not be fitting: from the delusion-word-said, from the mental-indeed, from the delusion, from the timira-marked, from the sensory, this separate declaration would not be fitting. &quot;From the delusion alone, from the spread, thus the declaration, from some specific trace&quot; — the ancient authoritative explanation he states for the refutation, &quot;that-again.&quot; With this, from his own explanation, the specific is indicated. This he does not tolerate: &quot;thus indeed.&quot; The &#x27;khalu&#x27;-word indicates the ridicule. With this he says: &quot;from the other delusion no specific trace is here obtained in the explanation, by which the separate declaration-worthiness would be.&quot; ### S9 — the convention-mind and the delusion [Objection:] &quot;The convention-mind, thus, becomes a coverer, if only the mind-raised [is the seen]; never, even at any time, is the seen — he — attributed to the general and the rest; in the attribution, even-equal, with this object, of the conventional, the separate taking.&quot; This he refutes, &quot;not-even&quot;; &quot;of the moon the twoness — the seen-ness alone, if this; of the many-grasped- common, even of the one, the seen-ness alone&quot; — the rule is equal. Thus, with this much, of the delusion-ness no one has any more, any specific, having established [which], even the delusion-specific-ness is not agreed by the text-author alone, declaring with the dvandva; he says &quot;having-superimposed, and the rest.&quot; In the simultaneous-support-ness [there is] the dvandva; and she is of the equal-own-form-two alone. The general, not swallowing all the specifics, operating, possessing even the other specific, wishing the specific, crooking [it], not separately obtained, the word-entry alone makes. &quot;Directly,&quot; with the world-cognition, clearly. For with the &#x27;dāntava&#x27;-&#x27;līvarda&#x27;-and-the-rest words alone the Ārya-worldly [people] declare the bulls; but with the &#x27;cow&#x27;-word the female-cows alone — thus alone the cognition. &quot;In &#x27;the cow-possessing this city&#x27;, when said, indeed, the curd-milk-prosperity alone manifests.&quot; &quot;The conventional-ness&quot;: &quot;of the conventional the marker is this-much alone&quot; — even by the other, not-wishing, this much alone is to be accepted. That marker, with the marked-word, he indicates, &quot;that-which (yattathā).&quot; And in this marker, with the manifestation-use two removed, in the non-possibility, our victory; with the non-possibility, again, the scattered [being] in the use of the other — with this intent: &gt; &quot;… with that reason (tena hetoḥ), the establishment, the un-refuted (abādhitā)&quot; and the rest. Otherwise, of the atoms the doing-of-effect-reason would be un-established.
